lesson.unitTitle: Everyday conversations with someone you love

introduction.goal: Check in, say how you feel, and keep a short exchange going.

line.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)
Do you want to rest? (to Knafeh)
Yes, I want to rest a little.

expressions.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)
How are you doing? (casual check-in to Fattoush)

introduction.usageNote: Check in, answer about yourself, then ask the other person back. Keep the speaker’s description separate from the listener’s address form. In this scene shū ʿāmel functions as a casual check-in; in another context it can ask what someone is doing.
introduction.dialectNote: Urban Palestinian teaching target. The casual check-in choice follows Palestinian-speaker feedback relayed and clarified by the owner on September 30, 2026. No universal claim about every Palestinian greeting is made. Feminine address and composed exchange are AI-assisted drafts; no native-expert review. Keep transliteration available: ʿ = ع; ā/ī/ū are long vowels. Jordanian alternatives are not introduced here.
introduction.recordingNote: Eight exercise prompts use AI-generated Jordanian-voice audio selected by the owner. Female mnīḥa retains the accepted heavier-m fallback. Dialogue and teaching cards have no attached recordings. Independent Palestinian pronunciation review and human recordings remain absent.

teachingCards.title: Start with a casual check-in

phrase.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)

teachingCards.note: Fattoush asks Knafeh how he is doing. In this greeting, answer about how you feel. When addressing Fattoush, use shū ʿāmle.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Fattoush. Greet Knafeh with a casual check-in.

teachingCards.title: Answer about yourself
teachingCards.note: Ana identifies the speaker. This form describes Knafeh; Fattoush says mnīḥa.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Knafeh. Fattoush checks in. Tell her you’re well.

teachingCards.title: Give a little detail
teachingCards.note: Fattoush is describing herself, so taʿbāne has a feminine ending. Shwayy keeps the tiredness mild.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Fattoush. Tell Knafeh you’re a little tired.

teachingCards.title: Keep the conversation going
teachingCards.note: You do not need to repeat the whole question. Inti addresses Fattoush; inta addresses Knafeh.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Knafeh. After answering, ask Fattoush the same question back.

teachingCards.title: Check in with Fattoush

phrase.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Fattoush)

teachingCards.note: The person you address changes the ending: ʿāmel to Knafeh, ʿāmle to Fattoush.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Knafeh. Start a casual check-in with Fattoush.

teachingCards.title: Offer a little rest

phrase.meaning: Do you want to rest? (to Knafeh)

teachingCards.note: Biddak asks what Knafeh wants; biddi says what you yourself want. Keep tirtāḥ with the question and artāḥ with your reply.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Fattoush. Knafeh is tired. Ask if he wants to rest.

teachingCards.title: Say what you need

phrase.meaning: Yes, I want to rest a little.

teachingCards.note: Biddi marks what the speaker wants. Reuse shwayy to ask for a little rest.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Knafeh. Accept Fattoush’s offer and say you want to rest a little.

recall.intent: Accepting a break and stating your wish to rest a little.

acceptedAnswers.meaning: Yes, I want to rest a little.
acceptedAnswers.rationale: Accepting a break and stating your wish to rest a little.

knownErrors.meaning: Do you want to rest? (to Knafeh)
knownErrors.rationale: This asks whether the other person wants to rest; the situation asks you to accept for yourself.

recall.hint: Begin with yes; say what you want to do, and keep “a little.”

variants.situation: After a long walk, Fattoush offers you a break. Accept and say you want to rest a little.
You have finished helping at home. Your friend suggests a break. Accept and say you want to rest a little.
